main_text.p: aut plures res significat, hoc modo: Paterfamilias cum filium heredem faceret, testamento uasa argetea uxori legauit: Tullius heres meus Terentiae uxori meae XXXpō do uasorum argenteorum data to,quę uolet.post mortem eius preciosa uasa & cælata magnificè illa petit. Tullius se, quæ uelit ipse, XXX pondo ei debere dicit. Cōstitutio est ex ambiguo. Eiusmodi con-trouersia illa est, An res empta, & tradita, emptoris tamen non sit, antequam pretium perfoluerit: de qua lurisconsulti in L. quod uendidi, 19.D.de contrah.empt. & L.

page.notes: The "«" marks in the right margin are printed line markers, one per line of the column, not text; they are not transcribed. The drawn hand beside "res em-" is an ornament, not text. Doubtful readings: "argetea" as printed (possibly argentea with a missing n); "cælata" and "ciū" as printed; signature "i 5" with the first character uncertain. The line-break in "Te / rentiæ" is joined to "Terentiae" as there is no printed hyphen. The printed "uolet.post" has no space after the full stop and is kept as printed.
